keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with driving punk energy
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

mainProgression.description: A propulsive three-chord minor key progression that drives the verses with relentless punk-influenced energy. The III-VII movement creates an uplifting anthemic quality against the minor tonic.

sectionProgressions.description: Synth-driven intro with Steve Stevens adding stabbing guitar accents over the main chord progression
Driving eighth-note power chord rhythm underneath Billy Idol's sneering vocal delivery
The anthemic 'more, more, more' chorus adds the G chord for a sense of resolution and grandeur
Ascending movement building tension before crashing back into the chorus

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Minor tonic providing dark, rebellious foundation
D (III) - Relative major adding brightness and anthemic lift
A (VII) - Subtonic chord creating forward momentum without classical dominant pull
G (VI) - Submediant adding emotional weight in the chorus turnaround

techniques.name: Driving Power Chord Rhythm
techniques.description: Fast eighth-note downstroke power chord strumming at 166 BPM, the backbone of Billy Idol's punk-influenced arena rock sound

notes: B5: X-2-4-4-X-X (root 5th string power chord)
D5: X-X-0-2-3-X (open D power chord voicing)
A5: X-0-2-2-X-X (open A power chord voicing)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (root 6th string power chord)
All chords played as tight, punchy power chords with palm muting between hits
Tempo is fast at 166 BPM - stamina is essential
sequence: Start with B5 power chord using consistent downstrokes
Maintain tight palm muting between chord strikes
Transition to D5 and A5 while keeping eighth-note rhythm locked
Add G5 in chorus sections for the four-chord pattern
Keep right hand loose but controlled at high tempo
tips: Build up speed gradually - start at 120 BPM and increase in 10 BPM increments
Focus on right-hand endurance as the fast tempo is demanding
Use slight palm muting to keep power chords tight and punchy
Let the chords ring slightly more in the chorus for contrast with the verse
details.progression: B5 - D5 - A5 (verse) / B5 - D5 - A5 - G5 (chorus)

techniques.name: Steve Stevens Lead Guitar Style
techniques.description: Flashy lead guitar fills and solo work combining punk attitude with technical proficiency, featuring whammy bar dives, harmonics, and fast pentatonic runs

notes: Lead fills use B minor pentatonic in the 7th position (7th-10th frets)
Artificial harmonics and whammy bar effects punctuate between vocal phrases
The solo features fast alternate picking runs with wide vibrato
Feedback and controlled noise are part of the sonic palette
Bends from D to E (minor 3rd to 4th) are signature sounds in the fills
sequence: Learn the basic B minor pentatonic box at the 7th fret
Practice the signature fill that answers the vocal the iconic vocal hook line
Work on whammy bar dive bombs and harmonic squeals
Build speed for the solo's alternate picking passages
Add vibrato and bending expression to match Stevens' style
tips: Stevens uses a Floyd Rose tremolo - a standard tremolo can approximate the effects
Focus on attitude and aggression rather than perfect note accuracy
Use the bridge pickup with moderate gain for the cutting lead tone
Practice feedback control by standing near your amp at moderate volume
details.progression: Lead fills over Bm - D - A progression

techniques.name: Palm-Muted Verse Riff
techniques.description: Tight palm-muted single-note riff on the low strings that underpins the verse sections, adding rhythmic drive beneath the power chords

notes: Root note (B) on the 5th string, 2nd fret with heavy palm muting
Alternates between palm-muted single notes and open power chord stabs
The muted notes create a percussive, chugging rhythm feel
Syncopated accents on the 'and' of beats 2 and 4 add punk attitude
sequence: Rest palm of right hand lightly on strings near the bridge
Play palm-muted eighth notes on the B root note
Lift palm muting for accented power chord hits
tips: The contrast between muted and open notes is what creates the dynamic
Keep palm muting consistent - too much kills the tone, too little loses the chug
Practice with a metronome to lock in the syncopated accents
Use the bridge pickup for maximum definition on muted notes
details.progression: Palm-muted B root with B5 - D5 - A5 stabs

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Iconic synth opening with Steve Stevens' guitar building in, establishing the driving tempo and dark minor key atmosphere
notes: Guitar enters after the synth intro with stabbing power chord accents
Build intensity gradually as the full band kicks in
Steve Stevens adds feedback and harmonic squeals over the progression
Lock in with the drum pattern for tight rhythmic foundation

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Driving verse with palm-muted rhythm guitar underneath Billy Idol's vocal, alternating between chugging single notes and power chord stabs
notes: Keep the rhythm tight and punchy with palm muting on the low strings
Accent the power chord changes on beat 1 of each new chord
Leave space for the vocal melody - don't overplay
The synth doubles the guitar progression for a massive wall of sound

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The explosive the signature chorus with open power chords ringing out and the added G chord creating anthemic resolution
notes: Open up the power chords - lift the palm muting for maximum sustain
The G chord adds a sense of arrival and completeness to the progression
Strumming intensity increases significantly from the verse
Steve Stevens adds soaring lead fills between vocal phrases

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Steve Stevens' blazing guitar solo featuring whammy bar effects, fast alternate picking, and aggressive bending over the verse progression
notes: Solo uses B minor pentatonic in the 7th position primarily
Features trademark whammy bar dive bombs and harmonic squeals
Fast alternate picking runs with aggressive vibrato
Builds to a climactic high bend before crashing back into the chorus

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Extended chorus repetition with building intensity, Steve Stevens adding increasingly wild lead embellishments over the anthemic chord progression
notes: Repeated chorus progression with maximum energy
Stevens adds increasingly wild lead guitar fills and feedback
The band builds to a massive crescendo
Final resolution on a sustained Bm power chord with feedback

guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for rhythm, neck humbucker for lead fills

effects.distortion: Marshall JCM800 natural overdrive with boost pedal for solos (Boss SD-1 or similar)
effects.delay: Short slapback delay (100-150ms) for lead parts
effects.other: Whammy bar (Floyd Rose or similar tremolo system) essential for Steve Stevens' lead style. Chorus pedal for subtle thickening on clean passages.

beginner.focus: Learn the three-chord verse progression using simplified open chord shapes
steps: Learn the Bm barre chord or simplified Bm (X-2-4-4-3-2)
Practice transitioning between Bm, D, and A at slow tempo
Work on basic downstroke eighth-note strumming at 100 BPM
Play along with the song using open chord versions
beginner.timeEstimate: 2-3 weeks to play along with basic chords

intermediate.focus: Master the power chord rhythm at full tempo with palm muting dynamics
steps: Convert chords to power chord voicings (B5, D5, A5, G5)
Practice palm-muted eighth-note rhythm at gradually increasing tempos
Build right-hand endurance to maintain 166 BPM for the full song
Add dynamic contrast between verse (palm muted) and chorus (open)
intermediate.timeEstimate: 3-5 weeks for confident rhythm guitar performance

advanced.focus: Add Steve Stevens-style lead fills and tackle the guitar solo
steps: Learn the signature lead fills that answer the vocal melody
Practice the guitar solo at half speed, building up gradually
Work on whammy bar techniques and artificial harmonics
Combine rhythm and lead parts for a complete performance
advanced.timeEstimate: 6-8 weeks for full performance with lead work

commonMistakes: Right hand fatigue from trying to maintain 166 BPM too soon - build up gradually
Losing the palm mute during fast chord transitions in the verse
Playing the chorus at the same dynamic level as the verse - contrast is essential
Rushing the tempo during the chorus energy buildup
practiceRoutine: Warm up with palm-muted eighth notes on the B5 power chord for 3 minutes
Practice verse progression (B5-D5-A5) at 120 BPM for 5 minutes
Add G5 for chorus pattern and drill transitions for 5 minutes
Increase tempo by 10 BPM increments toward 166 BPM target
Run through the full song structure at current comfortable tempo
focusAreas: Right-hand endurance for sustained fast downstroke strumming
Clean power chord transitions at high tempo
Dynamic contrast between palm-muted verse and open chorus
Tight rhythmic precision locked with the drum pattern
metronomeWork: Start at 120 BPM with palm-muted eighth-note power chords
Increase by 5-10 BPM per practice session
Target tempo: 166 BPM for full song performance
Practice with accents on beats 1 and 3 to develop the driving feel
